condEnd.pw: The lights flicker, hum, and stay on. Somewhere down the street, someone cheers.
condEnd.wt: The tap coughs, spits brown water, and then runs clear.
condEnd.fd: Food starts to flow into the markets again, and the worst of the hunger eases.
condEnd.rd: The barricades come down and traffic creeps back into the streets.
condEnd.sh: The shutters rattle up at the {shop}. People line up, grateful for something ordinary.
condEnd.wk: Work starts again. It feels strange and a little good to be needed somewhere.
condEnd.sc: The schools open their doors again.
condEnd.net: Your phone finds a signal and buzzes with a backlog of messages.
condEnd.air: The air clears. You notice it only because breathing stops being a thing you think about.

wch.l: Prepare: secure the home and gather supplies (2h)
wch.t: You work through it methodically: bring things in, tape and brace what you can, fill containers, charge everything.
You grab the essentials and go, locking the door behind you.

wch.l: Call your family and friends and make sure they are ready (30m)
wch.t: You work down your contacts, one call at a time, until everyone has heard it from you.
You go door to door. Some people are grateful. Some are already ready. Some need real help.

wch.l: That is all you can do. Wait and watch the news
wch.t: You settle in with the radio low and your phone in reach.

haz.mid: Italy|Albania|Algeria|Armenia|Azerbaijan|Georgia|Colombia|Venezuela|Panama|Honduras|Dominican Republic|Bolivia|Argentina|United States|China|India|Bhutan|Bangladesh|Myanmar|Iraq|Syria|Lebanon|Israel|Jordan|Palestine|Cyprus|Romania|Bulgaria|Croatia|Slovenia|Bosnia and Herzegovina|Serbia|North Macedonia|Montenegro|Kosovo|Portugal|Morocco|Uzbekistan|Turkmenistan|Kazakhstan|Ethiopia|Kenya|Tanzania|Malawi|Uganda|Rwanda|Burundi|Congo (DR)|Yemen|Eritrea|Djibouti|Fiji|Samoa|Mongolia|Canada|Russia|Cuba|Jamaica|Dominica|Saint Lucia|Saint Kitts and Nevis|Antigua and Barbuda|Saint Vincent and the Grenadines|Grenada|Iceland|Thailand|Laos|Vietnam|Malaysia|Timor-Leste|Egypt|Libya|Tunisia|Madagascar|Mozambique|Zambia
hit: The floor gives a short shudder. Cups chime on their shelves, then everything is still.
A low rumble passes under {city}, like a heavy truck that never arrives.
The ground rolls for several seconds. Pictures swing on their hooks and somewhere a window cracks.
A sharp jolt, then a long rolling sway. Car alarms start up all over {city}.
The earthquake hits like a hammer. Furniture lurches across the floor, plaster rains from the ceiling and the shaking goes on far longer than it should.
Everything moves at once: walls, floor, light fittings. The roar is deafening.
The ground heaves violently. Buildings groan and some of them do not hold. Dust blooms over {city} like smoke.
You cannot stand. The shaking tears at the city for what feels like a full minute, and the sound of collapsing concrete follows it.
The world breaks apart. The shaking is so violent that you are thrown to the ground, and the roar of falling buildings swallows every other sound.
Time stops being a thing. There is only the roar, the dust, the screaming, and the ground refusing to hold still.

acts.l: Drop, cover and hold on
acts.t: You drop to the floor, get under something solid and hold on until the world stops moving.

acts.l: Brace in a doorway
acts.t: You wedge yourself into the nearest doorframe and ride it out.

acts.l: Run for the exit
acts.t: You bolt for the door, stumbling through the shaking.

acts.l: Shield whoever is closest to you
acts.t: You throw yourself over the nearest person and hold on.

safe: You ride it out, shaking worse than the ground did.
When it stops, you are unhurt, breathing hard, and very aware of every sound.
You come through without a scratch, which feels almost unfair.
hurt: Something falls and finds you. You come out of it with {inj}.
You are thrown against a wall and end up with {inj}.
crit: A section of ceiling comes down on you. You remember dust, and then nothing.
Something heavy pins you in the dark. You hold on to the sound of your own breathing until hands finally find you.
inj: a deep gash on your scalp

warnT: Sirens wail along the coast. A tsunami warning has been issued: get to high ground now.
Your phone screams an emergency alert: a tsunami is expected. Down at the water, the sea has already begun to pull back.

wl.prep: Gather your documents and a bag, and head uphill (1h)

hit: The sea surges a metre higher than normal, swirls around the harbor and drains away again, leaving boats on their sides in the mud.
A wall of churning water pushes up the streets by the water, dragging cars and fish crates inland.
The wave comes in dark and fast, grinding through the waterfront. Everything low is swallowed.
The sea comes back as a wall. It flattens the waterfront, climbs the streets and keeps on going.
The ocean rises over {city} as if the land were an afterthought. The roar is beyond comprehension, and the water takes everything in its path.

acts.l: Run for high ground
acts.t: You run uphill without looking back, lungs burning, with half the street running beside you.

acts.l: Climb to the roof of a tall concrete building
acts.t: You take the stairs two at a time to the roof of the nearest solid tower.

acts.l: Try to drive away
acts.t: You jump into a car and join a road that is jammed solid within minutes.

acts.l: Go down to the shore to see what is happening
acts.t: You walk toward the water, curious, where the sea has drawn back and left the seabed bare.

safe: You make it to high ground, shaking, and watch the water do its work from a safe distance.
From the hill, the town looks like a toy someone has stirred with a spoon. You are alive, and so are the people around you.
hurt: The water catches you at the edge of the surge and drags you before it lets go. You come out of it with {inj}.
You are hit by something in the churn. When the water drains, you are left with {inj}.
crit: The water takes you. You do not remember how you came out of it, only the cold and the dark, and a stranger's hands.
The wave drags you under and spins you. When you wake, you are on a hillside under a coat that is not yours.

haz.hi: Indonesia|Philippines|Japan|Iceland|Ecuador|Guatemala|Papua New Guinea|Vanuatu|Nicaragua|El Salvador|Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
haz.mid: Italy|Costa Rica|Mexico|Chile|Peru|Colombia|Congo (DR)|Cabo Verde|Comoros|Dominica|Saint Kitts and Nevis|New Zealand|Russia|United States|Tonga|Solomon Islands|Greece
warnT: The volcano has been rumbling for days. The alert level has been raised, and officials are drawing up evacuation zones.
Ash falls lightly on {city}, and at night the mountain glows red. Officials urge everyone to be ready to leave at short notice.

wl.prep: Seal the windows, stock masks and pack a bag (2h)

hit: The mountain coughs a gray plume into the sky. Ash drifts over the rooftops like dirty snow, then thins out.
A real eruption: an ash column climbs over the mountain, and fine gray dust settles on everything in {city}.
The volcano erupts with a bang you feel in your chest. Ash falls thick enough to darken the day, and rocks rain onto the outskirts.
A massive eruption collapses into fast, scorching avalanches of gas and rock down the slopes. The sky turns night-dark at noon.
The volcano tears itself open. A black column climbs into the stratosphere, the sky goes dark, and fire runs down the mountain toward everything below.

acts.l: Leave the danger zone immediately
acts.t: You grab what you can and join the line of cars crawling away from the mountain.

acts.l: Seal the windows and stay in with a damp cloth over your face
acts.t: You tape the windows, soak a cloth and sit tight while the ash falls like a gray curtain.

acts.l: Help neighbors load up and leave first
acts.t: You spend the first precious minutes helping people carry things to the cars.

acts.l: Climb a hill for a better view
acts.t: You climb to see it for yourself, the heat and glow pulsing on your face.

safe: Ash in your hair, your lungs and your shoes, but you are unhurt.
You come out of it gritty, tired and alive.
hurt: You breathe too much ash and burn your throat raw. You come out with {inj}.
Falling debris catches you. You are left with {inj}.
crit: The heat and ash overwhelm you. You come to in an emergency tent with an oxygen mask over your face.
You black out choking on ash, and wake up in a convoy truck, coughing up gray.
inj: a head wound from falling rock

hit: A slope above the road slumps and slides across the tarmac in a slurry of mud and stones.
The hillside gives way with a wet roar, spilling mud down a lane and into the yards below.
A section of hillside comes down on the houses below it, carrying fences, cars and walls along.
The whole slope lets go. A river of mud and boulders buries a neighborhood in seconds.
The mountainside collapses in a roaring wall that wipes out everything beneath it.

acts.l: Run sideways, out of the path
acts.t: You run across the slope instead of down it, away from the roar.

acts.l: Get to the highest floor you can
acts.t: You take the stairs to the top floor and brace against the wall.

acts.l: Shout a warning to everyone, then run
acts.t: You yell until your voice cracks, then run with whoever is following.

acts.l: Freeze
acts.t: For a second your legs refuse to move.

safe: The mud stops a few metres from where you are standing. You do not move for a long time.
You are spattered, shaking and unhurt.
hurt: The mud knocks you off your feet and drags you a way. You are left with {inj}.
A flying rock clips you as you run. You end up with {inj}.
crit: The slide catches you and buries you to the chest. You are dug out, gray-faced and barely conscious.
You are swept under. The next thing you know is a hospital ceiling.

hit: A slab breaks off the slope above and powders across a ski run, well away from anyone.
An avalanche thunders down a gully and stops just short of the first houses, throwing up a cloud of snow.
A powerful avalanche tears through the upper edge of {city}, flattening sheds and burying the road.
The slope above {city} releases in a white roar. Snow buries an entire street.
A catastrophic avalanche buries part of {city}, a hundred metres of snow and splintered buildings in a few seconds.

acts.l: Get away from the slope and up to the top floor
acts.t: You grab what you can and take the stairs, away from the side that faces the mountain.

acts.l: Run for solid cover behind a stone wall
acts.t: You throw yourself behind the nearest stone wall and cover your face.

acts.l: Rush in to dig out whoever is buried
acts.t: You leave cover and dig with your hands, with a voice somewhere under the snow.

acts.l: Stay where you are
acts.t: You stay where you are, uncertain, as the white roar draws closer.

safe: The white cloud rolls past and settles. You are covered in powder and still breathing.
It stops short. You sit in the quiet with your heart running.
hurt: The edge of it catches you and buries you to the shoulders. You come out with {inj}.
A slab of snow knocks you flat. You get up with {inj}.
crit: The snow takes you under. You cannot move, cannot see, and then there are rescuers' probes and a shout.
You are buried. The cold and silence are total, and you will not remember how long it lasted.

hit: The pavement outside dips and cracks, and a hole the size of a car opens at the corner.
The road collapses without warning and swallows a parked car in a shower of dirt and pipe water.
A sinkhole opens beneath the building next door. Walls crack, and the whole block is told to get out.
The ground drops away beneath an entire building, which folds into the hole as the street disappears.
A huge collapse opens under {city}. A whole district sags into the void.

acts.l: Back away and shout for others to do the same
acts.t: You back away from the edge and yell until people clear the area.

acts.l: Run
acts.t: You do not think. You run, and the pavement behind you folds.

acts.l: Call emergency services and keep people back
acts.t: You make the call, then stand between the hole and everyone who wants a look.

safe: The edge crumbles a few steps from your feet. You stare into the hole.
It takes the car and the corner of the road, and spares you.
hurt: The ground gives way under one foot. You are pulled out with {inj}.
You are thrown by the collapse and end up with {inj}.
crit: The ground falls away under you. You are dragged out of the rubble by a rope and a lot of shouting.
You fall, and the world goes black.

warnT: A lake high above the valley has broken through its ice dam. A wall of water and boulders is racing down the river, and sirens sound in the valley.
Emergency calls go out: an outburst flood is coming down the valley. People near the river must climb to high ground.

wl.prep: Pack a bag and climb above the river (1h)
wl.evac: Move to the high ground right now (@10)

hit: A surge of silty gray water rushes down the river, higher than usual but contained.
A brown, boulder-heavy flood slams down the valley and rips out the footbridge.
A roaring flood of ice-cold water and rock tears down the river and takes the lower town.
A wall of water and boulders sweeps through the valley and erases the riverbank neighborhoods.
The valley disappears under a roaring flood of ice, boulders and mud.

acts.l: Climb to high ground
acts.t: You climb as fast as you can, above the river, and watch it roar past below.

acts.l: Get to the roof of the highest building
acts.t: You scramble to the roof of the highest building and hold on.

acts.l: Help people up the slope first
acts.t: You stay at the foot of the slope helping people up until the sound grows too loud.

acts.l: Go down to the river to look
acts.t: You walk toward the sound, drawn by it.

safe: You watch the flood from above, in awe and fear.
The water rages past below you, and you are on the right side of it.
hurt: The edge of the flood catches you. You come out of it with {inj}.
A boulder in the surge clips you and leaves you with {inj}.
crit: The water takes you off your feet and tumbles you downstream. You wake up on a hill, wrapped in foil blankets.
You are swept away and pulled out half a kilometre downstream, barely conscious.

warnT: The river authority has issued a flood warning. The rain keeps falling and the water keeps climbing.
Sandbags are stacking up at the end of the street. The forecast says more rain, and the river has already turned the color of tea.

wl.prep: Sandbag the doors and move your things upstairs (2h)

hit: The drains back up and water pools ankle-deep across the street, soaking shoes and basement stairs.
Water pours down the street and over the thresholds. Ground floors fill with muddy water.
The river tops its banks and floods the lower town. Cars drift down the road, and families climb to upper floors.
The flood swallows whole neighborhoods and rises past windows. Boats work the main street, and rescue helicopters hover overhead.
A wall of brown water covers {city}. Rooftops become islands, and the rescue services are overwhelmed.

acts.l: Move to higher ground or an upper floor
acts.t: You carry what you can upstairs and watch the water creep up the steps.

acts.l: Sandbag the door and hold the line
acts.t: You pile sandbags with the neighbors, passing them hand to hand as the water rises.

acts.l: Wade through the water to reach safety
acts.t: The water is colder and faster than it looks. You wade out holding onto walls and railings.

acts.l: Help carry elderly neighbors to safety
acts.t: You carry what and who you can, up the stairs and out of reach of the water.

safe: The water stops a step short of your door, or comes in and goes out again. You are unharmed and soaked.
You are cold, wet and entirely fine.
hurt: You slip in the current and are pulled under for a moment. You come out with {inj}.
Something sharp in the muddy water gets you. You end up with {inj}.
crit: The current pulls you off your feet and under, and the world turns brown and loud. A stranger pulls you out by the collar.
You are swept down the street and caught against a fence, half-drowned.
inj: a deep cut on your leg
a nasty fall and bruised hip

warnT: The sky upstream has turned black, and a flash flood warning has just come through. Water can arrive within minutes.
Thunder rolls over the hills. An emergency alert says a flash flood is on its way down the dry channels.

wl.prep: Move your things up and clear the low rooms (1h)

hit: A sudden torrent roars down the dry channel, brown with mud, and is gone within the hour.
A flash flood tears through the streets and drags cars down the road like toys.
A wall of mud-brown water roars through the lower town, taking cars, stalls and fences.
The flash flood tears through the district with a roar, ripping out walls and sweeping cars away.
A catastrophic flash flood smashes through {city} and turns its streets to rivers of rubble.

acts.l: Climb to higher ground
acts.t: You climb to a rooftop, a hillside or any place that water cannot reach.

acts.l: Get off the low roads and into a sturdy building
acts.t: You abandon the street and get inside the nearest solid building as the water arrives.

acts.l: Help someone stranded in a car
acts.t: You wade out with a rope and drag someone out of a car that is already moving.

acts.l: Try to cross the flooded street
acts.t: You step into what looks like shallow water, and it pulls at your knees.

safe: The water roars past and drops almost as fast as it rose. You are wet through and unhurt.
It is over in an hour. You are standing in mud, laughing for no good reason.
hurt: The surge knocks you off your feet. You end up with {inj}.
A piece of debris in the water slams into you. You are left with {inj}.
crit: The water sweeps you off your feet and tumbles you along the road. Someone grabs you, and then it is all noise.
You are swept away. A stranger finds you hours later, clinging to a fence.

warnT: The monsoon rain does not stop. Rivers are rising across the lowlands and the radio is warning of flooding by tomorrow.
A flood bulletin goes out: the monsoon rain has saturated the ground and the river will break its banks overnight.

wl.prep: Raise your belongings, stock water and seal the doors (2h)
wl.evac: Move to higher ground or the relief shelter (@18)

hit: The monsoon rain falls in sheets for a full day. Streets turn into canals, buses stop, and everyone wades.
Waterlogging spreads across the lowlands. Drains overflow, ground floors flood and the waterline in your lane climbs by the hour.
The monsoon rivers break their banks. Whole neighborhoods stand knee-deep in brown water, and boats appear on streets that had cars yesterday.
Devastating floods sweep through {city} and the villages around. Roofs poke out of the water, and the relief boats are overwhelmed.
A historic monsoon disaster drowns {city} and the plains around it. Millions are cut off, and the water keeps rising for days.

acts.l: Move to the upper floor or higher ground
acts.t: You move your family's things upstairs, one load at a time, with the water already at the door.

acts.l: Raise what you can and block the doors
acts.t: You stack everything on tables and beds, and block the door with sandbags and a plank.

acts.l: Join a neighbors' improvised boat rescue
acts.t: You and the neighbors push a flat boat through the lane, pulling people from windows.

acts.l: Stay put and hope the water stops
acts.t: You sit on the bed and watch the water rise up the legs.

safe: The water comes in and leaves again, taking a lot of things with it. You are unharmed.
You are soaked and exhausted and fine.
hurt: You slip in the flood and are swept off your feet. You come out with {inj}.
You cut yourself on submerged debris and end up with {inj}.
crit: The current knocks you off your feet and you go under. Strong hands pull you onto a boat.
You are swept away from your doorstep, half-drowned, before a rope catches you.
inj: a deep cut on your leg
a fever from the dirty water

haz.hi: Bahamas|Cuba|Haiti|Dominican Republic|Jamaica|Belize|Honduras|Nicaragua|Mexico|United States|Antigua and Barbuda|Barbados|Dominica|Grenada|Saint Kitts and Nevis|Saint Lucia|Saint Vincent and the Grenadines|Philippines|Taiwan|Japan|China|Vietnam|Bangladesh|India|Myanmar|Madagascar|Mozambique|Mauritius|Fiji|Vanuatu|Tonga|Samoa|Solomon Islands|Palau|Micronesia|Marshall Islands|Comoros
haz.mid: Guatemala|El Salvador|Trinidad and Tobago|South Korea|Sri Lanka|Oman|Australia|Seychelles|Tuvalu|Kiribati|Papua New Guinea|Thailand|Laos|Cambodia|Timor-Leste|Costa Rica|Pakistan|Canada
warnT: The weather service has named a {cyc} heading for the coast. The track points straight at {city}. Shops are boarding up and the roads out are filling.
A {cyc} warning has gone out. The sea is already restless, and the sky has the dull, bruised look that people here know to fear.

wl.prep: Board the windows, bring things in and fill containers (3h)

hit: Gale-force wind and lashing rain batter {city}, tearing branches loose and sending signs spinning down the street.
A {cyc} comes ashore. Roof tiles fly, trees come down, and the sea heaves against the harbor wall.
A powerful {cyc} hits. Roofs peel away, power lines whip in the wind, and a storm surge pushes into the low streets.
A severe {cyc} makes landfall with a roar. Buildings lose roofs and walls, the surge floods the waterfront and the wind does not let up for hours.
A catastrophic {cyc} tears through {city}. The wind strips buildings to their frames, the surge swallows the coast, and for hours the world is only noise and water.

acts.l: Shelter in the strongest interior room
acts.t: You pile mattresses in the strongest room and sit tight with the radio while the walls shudder.

acts.l: Stay upstairs with the windows boarded
acts.t: You stay above the waterline with shutters closed, listening to the building creak.

acts.l: Check on the neighbors in the eye of the storm
acts.t: In a strange, silent lull you rush out to check on neighbors, and race back as the wind returns.

acts.l: Go out to see it
acts.t: You step outside, and the wind knocks you sideways.

safe: The worst of it passes. You are shaken and unharmed.
You come through it hungry, tired and unhurt.
hurt: Something flies at you in the wind. You end up with {inj}.
You are knocked down in the surge and end up with {inj}.
crit: A part of the roof gives way above you, and then everything goes black.
You are hit by something big in the wind. You wake up in a crowded emergency ward.

warnT: The sirens go off, a rising howl over {city}. A tornado has been spotted on the ground, and it is heading this way.
Your phone shrieks a tornado warning. The sky has gone a sickly green, and the air is utterly still.

wl.prep: Get to the lowest interior room and gather supplies (30m)

hit: A narrow funnel touches down on the edge of town, tears up a field and a few fences, and lifts away.
A tornado clips the district, stripping roofs and tossing sheds around like dice.
A tornado carves a path through {city} with a freight-train roar. Houses lose their roofs, and cars tumble like toys.
A violent tornado cuts through {city}. Whole houses are lifted from their foundations, and the roar is the only thing you can hear.
A mile-wide tornado grinds across {city} and sweeps whole neighborhoods down to bare slabs.

acts.l: Get into the lowest, most interior room and cover your head
acts.t: You crawl into the bathtub, pull a mattress over yourself and hold on.

acts.l: Run for a sturdy public building
acts.t: You sprint for the nearest reinforced building and fall through the door.

acts.l: Try to outdrive it
acts.t: You jump in a car and try to outrun it. The road is packed.

acts.l: Stand at the window and film it
acts.t: You stand there with your phone, transfixed, as the funnel swells.

safe: The roar passes. You stay curled up for a long time, then peek out at a world rearranged.
You are not hurt. The house next door is gone.
hurt: Debris slams through the wall. You are left with {inj}.
You are flung across the room and end up with {inj}.
crit: The roof lifts, and the world fills with flying wood. You wake to hands pulling you from rubble.
You are thrown, and everything goes dark.

hit: A thunderstorm rolls over with fat drops, cracking thunder and a swirl of wind. It is loud, wet, and over in an hour.
Hail the size of marbles hammers {city}, shredding leaves and denting every car on the street.
A violent storm tears through with hail like golf balls and a gale that flings garden furniture across yards.
A line of severe storms rakes {city} with ferocious wind and heavy hail. Roofs, windows and cars take the worst.
A catastrophic supercell parks over {city}, with giant hail, flash flooding and winds that wreck whole streets.

acts.l: Get indoors and away from the windows
acts.t: You get inside, away from the glass, and watch the storm hammer the world from a safe distance.

acts.l: Take cover under the nearest solid roof
acts.t: You duck under the nearest solid cover and hold your bag over your head.

acts.l: Shelter in a car
acts.t: You dive into a parked car and the hail makes it a drum.

acts.l: Stay out and watch the lightning
acts.t: You stand in the doorway, entranced by the light show.

safe: The storm rolls away, leaving the street gleaming and strewn with leaves.
Wet, deafened and entirely unhurt.
hurt: A hailstone cracks you hard. You end up with {inj}.
You are hit by flying debris and end up with {inj}.
crit: A branch comes down on you out of nowhere. The next thing you know, you are being carried.
Lightning strikes close enough to throw you across the ground.
inj: a nasty bruise and a split lip
a shock burn on your arm

warnT: The weather service has issued a windstorm warning. Gusts are forecast to climb through the night, and people are told to secure everything loose.
A red wind alert has gone out for {city}. Schools are closing early and the transit services are suspending lines.

wl.prep: Secure loose items, board a window and stay near an inner wall (1h)

hit: A strong gale rattles every shutter and sends bins skittering down the road.
Gusts rip slates from roofs and bring branches down across the street. The lights flicker.
A damaging windstorm strips roofs and topples trees across {city}. Power lines are down all over.
A destructive windstorm flattens fences, uproots old trees and peels roofs from buildings in {city}.
A once-in-a-generation windstorm uproots forests and levels roofs. The grid is down for miles.

acts.l: Stay indoors, away from windows and big trees
acts.t: You stay in the inner room, away from the glass and listening to the roof grumble.

acts.l: Lash down loose things and board a window
acts.t: You tie, nail and weigh down everything the wind could throw.

acts.l: Check on neighbors between gusts
acts.t: You dash from door to door between gusts to make sure people are all right.

acts.l: Go out to see how bad it is
acts.t: You step out and the door is nearly wrenched from your hand.

safe: The howling dies down at last. You are untouched.
A tile or two missing and a tree down, and you are fine.
hurt: A flying slate catches you and you end up with {inj}.
You are blown off your feet and end up with {inj}.
crit: A falling branch brings you down. You wake in the hospital with a monitor beeping.
Something large and fast hits you out of the dark.

haz.mid: United States|Japan|South Korea|China|Afghanistan|Romania|Bulgaria|Serbia|Switzerland|Austria|Czechia|Slovakia|Hungary|Germany|Denmark|Slovenia|Croatia|Bosnia and Herzegovina|North Macedonia|Montenegro|Kosovo|Moldova|Uzbekistan|Türkiye|Iran|Nepal|Bhutan|North Korea|Albania|Italy|France|United Kingdom|Ireland|Netherlands|Belgium|Luxembourg|Andorra|Liechtenstein|San Marino|Monaco
warnT: A winter storm warning has been issued. Heavy snow and high winds are expected, and people are told to stay off the roads.
The sky has gone the color of old pewter. Forecasters say a blizzard is on its way, and the shelves at the {shop} are emptying fast.

wl.prep: Stock up, charge everything and bring in firewood (2h)

hit: A heavy snowfall muffles {city} and snarls the morning commute.
A proper snowstorm: thick snow, a biting wind, buses off the road and schools closed.
A blizzard blots out the world. Drifts climb the doors, and nobody is going anywhere.
A severe blizzard buries {city}. The wind howls, the temperature plunges, and stranded cars disappear into the white.
A historic blizzard buries {city} under drifts that cover cars and swallow whole streets. The cold is deadly.

acts.l: Stay home and keep warm
acts.t: You stay in, layer up and watch the world disappear into white.

acts.l: Dig a path to the door and stock up
acts.t: You shovel until your arms ache and carry in everything you can.

acts.l: Check on elderly neighbors
acts.t: You dig through to your neighbors' doors, in the dark and the howl, to see they are all right.

acts.l: Walk to the shop anyway
acts.t: You wrap up and head out into a world that is only wind and white.

safe: It snows itself out. You are warm, bored and unharmed.
The worst of it blows through and leaves a hushed, glittering world.
hurt: You slip on ice and fall hard. You are left with {inj}.
The cold gets into you. You end up with {inj}.
crit: You go down in the white and cannot get up. Someone finds you before the cold finishes the job.
Your body goes numb in the storm. You wake up in a warm bed, surrounded by blankets.

warnT: Freezing rain is on the way. The forecast says everything outdoors will be glazed with ice by morning, and power cuts are likely.
An ice storm warning has gone out: avoid the roads, bring in the plants, charge your phone.

wl.prep: Charge everything, fill the bath and gather blankets (1h)

hit: A glaze of freezing rain turns every surface to glass. {city} moves at a shuffle.
Freezing rain coats trees and wires. Branches crack like gunshots through the night.
An ice storm snaps trees and pulls down power lines all across {city}. The roads are skating rinks.
A severe ice storm brings down the grid. Thick ice crushes trees and roofs, and the city goes silent.
A catastrophic ice storm leaves {city} encased in ice. The grid collapses, and nobody can move.

acts.l: Stay in and keep warm
acts.t: You stay in, listen to the crack of falling branches and keep your boots by the door.

acts.l: Check for hazards and bring in firewood
acts.t: You test the roof and gutters, haul in firewood and fill the bath.

acts.l: Check on elderly neighbors
acts.t: You inch across the ice to the neighbors' doors, to bring blankets and check on them.

acts.l: Walk out to look at the damage
acts.t: You step out onto the glass and the world tilts under your shoes.

safe: It melts, drips and cracks, and you are fine.
The ice stays on the trees, and the world looks like a glass sculpture.
hurt: Your feet go out from under you. You are left with {inj}.
A branch cracks off and clips you. You end up with {inj}.
crit: You slip and hit your head on the ice. The world goes dark, and a neighbor finds you.
A falling limb knocks you flat.

warnT: A cold wave warning has gone out. Temperatures are set to plunge, and people are told to protect pipes, check on the elderly and keep warm.
The forecast is brutal: a deep freeze arriving tonight. Heaters are selling out.

wl.prep: Insulate the pipes, find blankets and stock hot food (2h)

hit: A cold snap bites: frost on every window, breath hanging in the air.
A hard freeze sets in. Pipes groan, puddles turn to iron, and heaters run all day.
A severe cold wave grips {city}. Water pipes burst, and the elderly are told to stay in.
A dangerous deep freeze settles over {city}. Ice cracks the roads, pipes burst by the hundreds, and the shelters fill.
A historic polar outbreak locks {city} in a killing cold. Even a short walk outdoors is dangerous.

acts.l: Stay in one warm room, layered up
acts.t: You close off all but one room, layer on everything you own and keep the kettle busy.

acts.l: Protect the pipes and the heating
acts.t: You wrap pipes, leave taps dripping and shut up the draughts.

acts.l: Check on elderly neighbors
acts.t: You knock on the doors of old people who might not ask for help.

acts.l: Carry on as normal
acts.t: You go out as usual, underdressed, and the cold finds every gap.

safe: The cold bites and finally eases. You are fine.
You huddle in blankets, count the hours and make it through.
hurt: The cold gets you. You end up with {inj}.
You slip on frozen ground and end up with {inj}.
crit: The cold gets deep into you. You are found shivering uncontrollably and rushed to a warm ward.
Your hands and feet stop obeying you. It takes a long time to warm up.
inj: a broken wrist from an icy fall

warnT: A heat warning has been issued. Temperatures are set to soar for days, and people are told to drink water, stay inside and check on neighbors.
The forecast is for a punishing heatwave. Fans and ice are sold out at the {shop}, and the radio keeps repeating one word: hydrate.

wl.prep: Buy ice, fill bottles and set up the coolest room (1h)

hit: A hot spell sits on {city}, sticky and still, and everyone reaches for a fan.
A heatwave pushes temperatures well past normal. The pavement shimmers and the afternoon streets empty.
A severe heatwave presses down for days. The nights bring no relief, and ambulances are busy with heat exhaustion.
A deadly heat dome parks over {city}. Power demand maxes out the grid, hospitals fill, and the streets are silent by noon.
A record-shattering heat catastrophe cooks {city}. Metal burns your hand, the grid struggles, and it is too hot to be safe anywhere without cooling.

acts.l: Stay in the coolest room and keep drinking water
acts.t: You close the shutters, wet a cloth for your neck and sip water through the worst hours.

acts.l: Cool off at a pool, river or shaded public space
acts.t: You lie in the water and watch the sky go white with heat.

acts.l: Check on elderly neighbors and bring them water
acts.t: You make a round of doors with a jug of cold water, and find people who needed it.

acts.l: Go out and carry on as normal
acts.t: You head out into the heat as if it were any day.

safe: The heat finally breaks. You are tired, sticky and unharmed.
You get through it on water, shade and willpower.
hurt: The heat catches up with you. You come out with {inj}.
You stay out too long and end up with {inj}.
crit: The heat flattens you. You collapse and wake up in a cooling tent with an IV in your arm.
You pass out in the heat. A stranger pours water over you until the ambulance comes.

warnT: A brown wall is climbing the horizon. A dust storm warning has been issued: get inside and shut the windows.
The air has gone the color of weak tea. A sandstorm is on the way, and the radio is telling everyone to cover their faces.

wl.prep: Seal the windows and get masks and water ready (1h)

hit: A haze of fine dust blows through and tints the sky orange.
A sandstorm rolls in like a brown wall, and the sun disappears at once.
A heavy sandstorm swallows {city}. Visibility drops to a few metres, and the grit finds every crack in the building.
A severe sandstorm blacks out the afternoon. The wind is a constant roar of grit, and the world is a dim orange.
A historic dust storm buries {city} under drifting sand. For a day the sky is the color of rust, and breathing outside is dangerous.

acts.l: Get inside and seal every gap
acts.t: You close the shutters, stuff towels in the cracks and sit in the dim brown light.

acts.l: Cover your face and wait it out
acts.t: You tie a wet cloth over your face and crouch against a wall, away from the wind.

acts.l: Try to drive home through it
acts.t: You drive in near-darkness, creeping through the swirling brown.

acts.l: Help bring in a neighbor's animals and washing
acts.t: You help the neighbors get everything in before the dust arrives.

safe: It passes. You cough up grit for an hour and are otherwise fine.
Your hair, teeth and pockets are full of sand. That is all.
hurt: Sand and wind take a toll. You end up with {inj}.
You trip in the blinding dust and end up with {inj}.
crit: You inhale dust until your chest feels like it is burning. You wake up in an emergency tent breathing oxygen.
You are lost in the whiteout until someone finds you.
inj: a bad cough that will not stop

warnT: Smoke on the horizon. A wildfire is spreading toward {city}, and the authorities have told people to be ready to leave.
The sky turns copper and ash starts to fall like snow. An evacuation warning has come through: pack and be ready to go.

wl.prep: Clear the yard, soak the roof and pack a bag (2h)

hit: A brush fire flares at the edge of town and is beaten back by firefighters before it reaches the first houses.
A wildfire races across the dry hills and sends ash drifting over {city}. A few homes at the edge are lost.
A major wildfire reaches the outskirts. Flames leap the road, the sky turns orange, and entire streets are told to evacuate.
A firestorm sweeps into {city}, driven by a hot wind. Houses go up like torches.
A catastrophic firestorm engulfs {city} with a roar like a jet engine. The sky is black, and the fire outruns cars.

acts.l: Evacuate right now
acts.t: You grab the bag, the people and the car, and drive through the orange gloom with the fire in the mirror.

acts.l: Help neighbors load their cars before you go
acts.t: You spend precious minutes helping neighbors load and leave, then you go too.

acts.l: Shelter in a cleared area or open water
acts.t: You head for the lake and wade in, wet cloth over your face, and watch the hill burn.

acts.l: Stay and defend the house with a hose
acts.t: You stay behind with a hose and wet blankets, with embers swirling around you.

safe: The fire passes. You are hacking and sooty but unhurt.
You get out with the clothes on your back and a lot of ash in your hair.
hurt: The heat and smoke get to you. You come out with {inj}.
You are caught by a flash of flame and end up with {inj}.
crit: Smoke closes over you and everything goes dark. A firefighter drags you from the fumes.
You are overcome by smoke and heat, and come to on a stretcher.
inj: singed hair and a scorched throat

hit: It has not rained in weeks. The ground is cracking, and the taps run weaker each day.
The dry spell drags on. Water restrictions begin, and the price of vegetables creeps up.
A serious drought tightens its grip. Wells run low, crops fail and the water is rationed.
A severe drought has emptied the reservoirs. Water arrives by tanker, and food prices soar.
A historic drought has turned the countryside to dust. Hunger spreads, the wells are dry, and families are leaving for the cities.

acts.l: Conserve every drop and stockpile what you can
acts.t: You catch the shower water, reuse everything and fill every container you own.

acts.l: Pay for clean water deliveries (@12)
acts.t: You pay for a delivery and ration it with a cup and a conscience.

acts.l: Queue at the distribution point every day
acts.t: You spend your mornings in line at the tanker with a collection of jugs and neighbors.

acts.l: Carry on as usual
acts.t: You decide it will probably rain soon.

safe: You get through it thin, thirsty and unharmed.
The rain finally comes, and you stand in it.
hurt: The hardship takes a toll on your body. You end up with {inj}.
Poor water and thin meals leave you with {inj}.
crit: You collapse from thirst and hunger. You wake at a feeding station with a drip in your arm.
Your body gives out. A neighbor spots you and carries you to the clinic.
inj: a stomach infection from bad water

hit: A few locusts, then a few more. Farmers eye the sky with a tired, practiced worry.
Hoppers crawl across the fields in hungry bands, and the market stalls grow thin.
A swarm blackens the sky for an hour, devouring gardens, crops and the fruit on every tree.
A devastating swarm, tens of kilometres wide, strips the land bare. The harvest is gone.
A plague of locusts darkens the land in wave after wave. Entire harvests are destroyed, and hunger looms.

acts.l: Join the neighbors banging pots to scare them off
acts.t: You join the din, banging pots with half the street as the cloud passes overhead.

acts.l: Buy and store food before prices rise (@15)
acts.t: You buy what you can while the shelves are still full.

acts.l: Cover the garden and keep everything indoors
acts.t: You cover everything you can and seal the house against the whirring, rustling cloud.

acts.l: Wait it out
acts.t: You sit in the dim light with the noise of the swarm at the roof.

safe: The swarm passes. The garden is a ruin, but you are unhurt.
They eat everything outside and spare you.
hurt: The hardship takes a toll. You end up with {inj}.
You fall while chasing the swarm and end up with {inj}.
crit: Weeks of hunger catch up with you. You collapse and wake at a feeding point.
You are brought low by hunger and illness.

hit: A cluster of food poisoning at a local stall puts a dozen people in bed. Inspectors close it down.
A seasonal illness sweeps through {city}. Half the people you meet are sniffling, and the clinic queue spills outside.
An epidemic takes hold. Clinics are crowded, masks reappear, and rumors spread faster than the illness.
A severe epidemic overwhelms the hospitals. Schools close, markets thin out and people stay behind closed doors.
A fast-spreading pandemic wave locks {city} down. Hospitals are overrun, streets are empty, and everyone is afraid.

acts.l: Wash up, mask up and keep your distance
acts.t: You wash obsessively, wear a mask, and keep your distance from everyone, even those you love.

acts.l: Isolate at home and avoid everyone
acts.t: You shut the door and stay in, and the days stretch out. The quiet gets heavy.

acts.l: Volunteer at the clinic
acts.t: You turn up at the clinic in a mask and gloves and do whatever they hand you.

acts.l: Carry on as usual
acts.t: You decide it is probably overblown and go about your business.

safe: You stay well while everyone around you coughs.
You come through without catching it.
hurt: You catch it. You come down with {inj}.
It finds you in the end. You spend days with {inj}.
crit: It hits you hard. The fever climbs and the world blurs, and you wake up in a ward with oxygen tubes.
You are very sick. For days you float in and out of a feverish haze.
inj: a high fever and aching bones
a stomach illness that will not let go

warnT: Scientists warn that a huge solar eruption has been flung toward Earth. A geomagnetic storm is expected, and the grid operators are on alert.
Space-weather agencies have raised an alert: a big solar flare is on the way, and satellites and power grids may be affected.

wl.prep: Charge everything, fill containers and gather torches (1h)

hit: The night sky ripples green and red. Strangers stand in the street with their phones out, grinning at the northern lights.
A radio blackout cuts GPS and radio for hours. The aurora glows far from the poles, and nobody quite knows what to make of it.
A geomagnetic storm trips transformers and blacks out parts of {city}. The sky is on fire with color.
A severe geomagnetic storm collapses sections of the grid. Satellites falter and the sky glows red.
An extreme solar superstorm burns out transformers across the continent. The lights go out and stay out, and the sky burns green, red and violet all night.

acts.l: Unplug your electronics and wait it out
acts.t: You unplug everything, light a candle and wait.

acts.l: Go outside and watch the sky
acts.t: You step out into the street and look up, with an entire neighborhood staring skyward.

acts.l: Fill the bath, charge what you can and gather light
acts.t: You charge phones, fill the tub and gather candles.

acts.l: Ignore it and go about your night
acts.t: You shrug it off and carry on, until the lights go.

safe: The sky puts on a show. It is quietly unforgettable.
You are fine, if a bit out of your depth.
hurt: You trip in the dark and end up with {inj}.
In the blackout, you end up with {inj}.
crit: In the dark and chaos, you are badly hurt. A stranger helps you to a clinic.
A fall in the blackout leaves you unconscious until morning.

hit: A fireball streaks across the sky, brighter than the moon, and breaks into pieces. Then silence. Then every phone in {city} lights up.
A sonic boom rattles every window in {city}. A bright streak was seen in the sky, and a few panes cracked.
A meteor explodes over {city} with a flash brighter than the sun. The shockwave smashes windows and throws people off their feet.
A meteorite slams into the outskirts of {city}, throwing up a fireball and a shockwave that levels buildings.
An impact tears a crater into {city}. The shockwave rolls outward and flattens everything in its way.

acts.l: Get down and away from the windows
acts.t: You throw yourself to the floor, away from the glass, and cover your head.

acts.l: Stand and stare at the sky
acts.t: You stand there, awestruck, as the light fades and a rumble builds.

acts.l: Run for the nearest sturdy building
acts.t: You run for the nearest solid roof as the shockwave rolls closer.

acts.l: Film it
acts.t: You hold your phone up, with the whole sky full of light.

safe: The boom rolls past. You are shaken and delighted and slightly deaf.
Nobody will believe your story. You have the video to prove it.
hurt: The shockwave hits you hard. You end up with {inj}.
Flying glass finds you. You are left with {inj}.
crit: The shockwave throws you across the room. You wake in the ambulance, deaf and bleeding.
The light blinds you, and then comes the blast.

ev.text: {neigh}, next door, knocks. Their face is gray. They are out of food, and there are children in the house.

choices.label: Share what you have (@6)
choices.text: You split what you have. {neigh} cries a little and tries to hide it.

choices.label: Walk them to the relief point (1h)
choices.text: You go together. It is easier with company.

choices.label: Apologize. You need your own supplies
choices.text: You close the door. It sits badly with you for the rest of the day.

ev.text: The line at the relief point wraps around the block. People are patient, and then they are not.

choices.label: Wait your turn (2h)
choices.text: It takes two hours and a lot of small talk. You leave with a bag of food and water.

win.text: The line moves, and volunteers hand you hot food and bottled water.

lose.text: The supplies run out three people ahead of you.

choices.label: Help the volunteers keep order (1h)
choices.text: You calm a pushing match and form the line into a snake.

choices.label: Skip it and find food elsewhere
choices.text: You walk away from the queue and a rumble in your stomach.

ev.text: A rumor tears through the neighborhood: a second wave is coming, or the dam is cracking, or looters are on the way. Everyone starts packing.

choices.label: Check an official source before reacting (30m)
choices.text: You listen for the official line.

win.text: It is false. You calm people down and a few thank you.

lose.text: The radio is vague. You end up as scared as before.

choices.label: Pass it on, just in case
choices.text: You warn everyone. By evening, it is clear it was a rumor, and you feel foolish.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: You choose to wait. Nothing happens, this time.

ev.text: A small child stands alone on the corner, crying, in a coat three sizes too big.

choices.label: Stay with them and flag down help (1h)
choices.text: You stay with them until a distraught parent runs up and sobs.

choices.label: Carry them to the relief point (1h)
choices.text: Volunteers know what to do. You hand the child over and leave with your heart pounding.

choices.label: Walk on. You cannot deal with this
choices.text: You keep walking, and it follows you down the street.

ev.text: The shutter of the {shop} hangs open. Nobody is inside, and the shelves are full.

choices.label: Take only what you need to eat
choices.text: You take bread and water and tell yourself it is survival. The guilt keeps you company.

win.text: Nobody sees you.

lose.text: A patrol shouts at you. You drop everything and run.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.text: You walk on. You are hungry, and a bit proud.

choices.label: Guard the shop until the owner returns (2h)
choices.text: The owner returns at dusk, hugs you and presses food into your hands.

ev.text: A TV crew is working the street. A reporter points a microphone in your direction.

choices.label: Tell it straight (30m)
choices.text: You tell it plainly.

win.text: Your words land. A few neighbors say they saw you on the news.

lose.text: You stumble over the words and wish you had kept quiet.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: You shake your head and carry on.

ev.text: Sorting through the damage, something turns up under a layer of dust: {keepsake}.

choices.label: Hold on to it (30m)
choices.text: You turn it over in your hands. It is a small thing, and it is everything.

choices.label: Put it somewhere safe and keep sorting
choices.text: You tuck it into a pocket and go back to the work.

ev.text: A vendor is charging triple for water and batteries. Behind you, a woman is counting coins with an unhappy face.

choices.label: Pay it (@12)
choices.text: You pay and walk away with a sour taste.

choices.label: Argue the price down
choices.text: You argue, politely and then less so.

win.text: The vendor sighs and drops the price. The woman behind you nods her thanks.

lose.text: He shrugs. Take it or leave it.

choices.label: Walk to another stall (1h)
choices.text: You walk, and find a stall selling at a fair price. It is a small win.

ev.text: A neighbor has dragged out a generator and is charging phones for a few coins. There is a queue, and a few kind words.

choices.label: Charge your phone (@2)
choices.text: Your phone wakes with a buzz of messages. It is a relief to hear from people.

choices.label: Help with the fuel run (2h)
choices.text: You and a few others haul fuel cans through the dark. The generator keeps humming.

choices.label: Not today
choices.text: You pass.

ev.text: You realize you have not seen the old person at the end of your street since the disaster. The shutters are closed.

choices.label: Knock and check on them (30m)
choices.text: You knock until you hear a thin voice.

win.text: They are shaken but fine, and so glad to see someone that they hold your hand for a long time.

lose.text: They are weak and unwell. You call for help and stay until it arrives.

choices.label: Tell someone else to check
choices.text: You mention it to a volunteer and hope that is enough.

ev.text: {friend} calls. "I just saw the news. Are you okay? I could not get through."

choices.label: Talk it through (1h)
choices.text: You tell them everything. At the end, you feel lighter.

choices.label: Keep it short. You are fine
choices.text: You say you are okay, and mostly mean it.

ev.text: A loss adjuster is on the phone. Sound polite, patient, and slightly bored.

choices.label: Document everything carefully (1h)
choices.text: You go through photos, receipts, damage reports. It is tedious and it helps.

win.text: The assessor is satisfied and pays a bonus on top.

lose.text: Some of your paperwork is missing, and the claim shrinks.

ev.text: The street organizes an impromptu meal in the road. Every household brings something. Someone has found a guitar.

choices.label: Join in (3h)
choices.text: It is the kind of evening that gets remembered. People who do not usually speak are talking over each other.

choices.label: Cook something to bring (@6, 2h)
choices.text: Your dish is gone in minutes, and people ask for the recipe.

choices.label: Stay in
choices.text: You listen to the music through the wall.

ev.text: A sudden noise, and your body reacts before you do. For a few seconds, you are right back in it.

choices.label: Breathe through it (30m)
choices.text: You count your breath and name things you can see. It fades.

choices.label: Call someone (1h)
choices.text: You call someone who picks up right away.

choices.label: Push it down
choices.text: You tell yourself it is over. The feeling tightens in your chest.

ev.text: The ground shakes again. A hard jolt, the rattle of glass, and a scream from down the street.

choices.label: Drop, cover and hold on
choices.text: It is brief and enormous. You wait it out with your heart in your throat.

choices.label: Run outside
choices.text: You burst out into the street, with half the neighborhood doing the same.

win.text: It stops. You stand in the road with your neighbors, laughing in a shaky way.

lose.text: A tile slides off the roof and clips your shoulder.

ev.text: A sharp smell of gas drifts through the street. A hiss comes from a broken pipe by the corner.

choices.label: Warn everyone and call it in (30m)
choices.text: You knock on doors and make the call. The crews arrive and shut it off.

choices.label: Stay away and tell nobody
choices.text: You leave. It nags at you.

ev.text: An inspector in a hard hat circles your building and marks the wall with spray paint. Yellow means look again. You cannot read the symbol.

choices.label: Ask for the details (30m)
choices.text: You ask politely, then not so politely.

win.text: It is only cosmetic. You may stay.

lose.text: It is not safe for now. You will have to leave.

choices.label: Pack up and leave to be safe
choices.text: You are not taking chances.

ev.text: The tap water has turned cloudy and smells wrong. The radio warns people to boil everything.

choices.label: Boil and store a big batch (1h)
choices.text: You boil, cool and fill every container. It is boring, and it is worth it.

choices.label: Drink it anyway
choices.text: You take a risk, because you are thirsty.

win.text: It tastes like a swimming pool and does you no harm.

lose.text: Your stomach turns by evening. It is a rough night.

ev.text: A dark bloom is spreading up the damp walls, and the smell is thick.

choices.label: Scrub and ventilate (2h)
choices.text: You scrub with bleach, open every window and mop until your arms ache.

win.text: The air clears and the walls begin to dry.

lose.text: It keeps coming back, and your chest feels tight.

choices.label: Leave it for now
choices.text: You close the door on the room.

ev.text: A neighbor is stranded on the upper floor of their flooded house, shouting for help through the window.

choices.label: Wade over with a rope and a plank (1h)
choices.text: You tie off, test each step and reach out.

win.text: You get them out. They are crying and hugging you at the same time.

lose.text: The current is too strong. You retreat, soaked, and call the rescue boats.

choices.label: Call the rescue boats and wait with them by phone (30m)
choices.text: You keep them talking until the boat arrives.

ev.text: Embers are blowing in the wind. A spot fire has caught in the dry grass beside the road.

choices.label: Beat it out with wet sacks (1h)
choices.text: You and a few neighbors swing wet sacks until the little fire is dead.

win.text: The spot fire dies. People cheer, hoarse and sooty.

lose.text: It spreads, and the firefighters take over. You are scorched.

choices.label: Call it in and stay clear
choices.text: You step away and make the call.

ev.text: Ash is piling on the roofs. Wet, it is as heavy as concrete, and a few have already caved in.

choices.label: Sweep your roof clear (2h)
choices.text: You climb up with a broom and a wet cloth over your face, and sweep until your arms shake.

win.text: The roof holds. You come down gray from head to toe.

lose.text: You slip on the wet ash and bruise yourself badly.

choices.label: Pay someone to do it (@10)
choices.text: A neighbor with a ladder and a bucket takes the money and the job.

ev.text: The air is thick and acrid. There is a queue for masks at the pharmacy, and the pharmacist is rationing.

choices.label: Wait for a mask (1h)
choices.text: You wait, and get a mask and a lecture about how to wear it.

win.text: It fits well enough, and your lungs thank you.

lose.text: They run out. You tie a wet cloth around your face.

choices.label: Improvise with a wet scarf
choices.text: It is not perfect.

ev.text: A pipe bursts inside the wall. Water is pouring through the ceiling and freezing on the floor.

choices.label: Shut the valve and mop up (1h)
choices.text: You find the valve, wrestle it shut and mop frantically.

win.text: The flow stops. The damage is limited.

lose.text: Water gets everywhere before you stop it.

choices.label: Call a plumber (@10)
choices.text: You pay a lot to someone with a van.

ev.text: A neighbor has run a generator inside to keep warm. You smell fumes in the stairwell, and you recognise the headache.

choices.label: Get everyone out and open the windows
choices.text: You bang on doors and drag people into the cold. It is the right call, and it may have saved lives.

choices.label: Tell them to turn it off and go back to sleep
choices.text: You get a headache and no sleep.

ev.text: A car is stuck in a drift at the end of the road, engine dead, and someone is inside, shivering.

choices.label: Dig it out and bring them in (2h)
choices.text: You dig for an hour and get them out, blue-lipped and apologetic.

win.text: You warm them with tea and blankets. They will not forget it.

lose.text: You cannot move the car, but you get the person to safety.

choices.label: Call for help
choices.text: You call and wait until the plough arrives.

ev.text: It is dangerously hot, and an elderly neighbor has not come out for water in two days.

choices.label: Knock and bring a jug of cold water
choices.text: You knock until the door opens.

win.text: They are dehydrated but fine. You sit with them until their color returns.

lose.text: They are unwell. You call an ambulance and hold their hand.

choices.label: Leave them to it
choices.text: You keep the shutters closed.

ev.text: Your cooling gives out in the worst of the heat. The room becomes an oven.

choices.label: Go to a cooler public place (2h)
choices.text: You sit in an air-conditioned lobby with a bottle of water.

win.text: A kind guard pretends not to notice.

lose.text: It is packed with people doing the same.

choices.label: Soak a sheet and lie under the fan
choices.text: You do it the old-fashioned way. It is almost bearable.

ev.text: A water tanker has arrived at the end of the street, and a quarter of the neighborhood has descended with buckets.

choices.label: Join the line (2h)
choices.text: You wait and fill what you can.

win.text: Your containers fill. It tastes like victory.

lose.text: The tank runs dry just before your turn.

choices.label: Help the elderly carry their buckets (1h)
choices.text: You carry buckets until your arms are numb.

ev.text: The shared well has run dry. People stand around it, peering in.

choices.label: Join the group looking for a new source (3h)
choices.text: You walk for hours with a group of neighbors, and you find a spring a few kilometres out.

win.text: You carry water home that night.

lose.text: You come home empty-handed and exhausted.

choices.label: Pay for water instead (@12)
choices.text: It is expensive, and it is wet.

ev.text: A rustling cloud blots out the sun. Locusts, millions of them, land on the street, the trees and the roofs with a sound like heavy rain.

choices.label: Run indoors and seal everything (30m)
choices.text: You slam the door on a world gone brown and moving.

choices.label: Bang pots with the neighbors (1h)
choices.text: The whole street makes a racket. It does little except to bring people together.

choices.label: Gather them to cook (1h)
choices.text: You collect a bag. Fried with salt and chili, they are surprisingly good.

ev.text: The clinic queue spills out the door. A nurse is walking the line with a clipboard and a mask.

choices.label: Wait to be checked (3h)
choices.text: You wait. It is crowded and silent.

win.text: You are cleared. Relief.

lose.text: You are told to go home and wait, which is not what you hoped.

choices.label: Help the nurse manage the line (2h)
choices.text: You carry water, hand out forms and keep people calm.

choices.label: Stay home and monitor it yourself
choices.text: You wait it out at home.

ev.text: A volunteer in a mask rings your bell. Someone in your building has tested positive, and you should stay in for a while.

choices.label: Stay in as asked
choices.text: You stay in for days with a stack of books and a growing talent for staring at walls.

choices.label: Go out for essentials only
choices.text: You slip out in a mask for essentials, ashamed and nervous.

ev.text: A cousin forwards a message about a miracle cure. It is a home remedy, and half the neighborhood is trying it.

choices.label: Look into it properly (1h)
choices.text: You go looking for the facts.

win.text: It is nonsense. You post the facts, and some people listen.

lose.text: It is hard to tell. You do nothing and feel useless.

choices.label: Try it, just in case
choices.text: It tastes awful, and nothing happens.

choices.label: Delete the message
choices.text: You ignore it.

ev.text: The cash machines are down, the card readers are dead, and the {shop} is accepting only coins and handshakes.

choices.label: Pay with whatever cash you have
choices.text: You scrape together what you have.

choices.label: Trade something or work it off (1h)
choices.text: You carry crates for a bag of food. The old way works.

win.text: Everyone is oddly friendly.

lose.text: Nobody needs help today.

ev.text: People are searching the fields for fragments of the meteorite. Collectors are already offering money.

choices.label: Join the search (3h)
choices.text: You walk the fields with a hundred other hopefuls.

win.text: You find a dark, heavy stone with a glossy crust. A dealer pays you well.

lose.text: You find a lot of ordinary rocks and a sunburn.

choices.label: Stay home and enjoy the quiet
choices.text: You leave it to the hunters.

ev.text: The sea draws back from the shore, farther and farther, leaving the harbor floor bare. Dozens of people walk out onto it with their phones in their hands.

choices.label: Run up the hill and shout for everyone to follow
choices.text: You run, yelling until your voice goes. Many follow you, and the second wave comes in minutes.

choices.label: Go up the hill, but do not stop for anyone
choices.text: You save yourself and watch from above, with a knot in your stomach.

ev.text: A search team needs every pair of hands. A hiker is believed to be buried, and every minute counts.

choices.label: Join the search line, probing the snow (3h)
choices.text: You stand shoulder to shoulder, probing in silence.

win.text: A shout goes up. They dig out a living, shaking hiker, and everyone cries.

lose.text: They find the body at dusk. Nobody speaks on the walk back.

choices.label: Bring hot drinks and blankets to the search teams (2h)
choices.text: You make yourself useful on the edge, which helps.

ev.text: The sirens start again. A second storm cell is bearing down while everything is still broken.

choices.label: Take cover immediately
choices.text: You get back down into the interior room. This time, it passes to the side.

choices.label: Check on neighbors first, then take cover
choices.text: You bang on doors on the way and make it down just in time.

ev.text: Night falls on a city without lights. It is utterly dark, and it is eerily quiet.

choices.label: Light a candle and read (2h)
choices.text: The small flame makes the dark feel friendlier. You read until the page blurs.

choices.label: Sit on the step and talk with neighbors (2h)
choices.text: Voices in the dark, and a surprising number of stars.

ev.text: The children on your street have turned the wreckage into a playground, and one of them is selling invisible tickets to the show.

choices.label: Buy a ticket (@1)
choices.text: The show is chaotic and wonderful. You clap until your hands sting.

choices.label: Watch from a distance
choices.text: You smile at the small, stubborn normality of it.

ev.text: People gather in the square with candles for those who did not make it. Someone reads the names.

choices.label: Go and stand with them (2h)
choices.text: It is quiet and heavy. When it is over, nobody wants to leave first.

choices.label: Stay home
choices.text: You listen to the faint singing through the window.

prep.txt: You read through the civil-protection leaflets and the maps of evacuation routes. For the first time, the risks around {city} stop being abstract.
You agree on a meeting place, an out-of-town contact and a way to reach each other when the phones fail. It feels a little silly, and a lot better afterwards.
Documents in a sealed bag, a torch, a first-aid kit, a change of clothes, a phone charger, cash and a bottle of water. You put it by the door.

prep.l: Stock water and food for a few days (@20)
prep.txt: Tins, rice, biscuits and as much bottled water as you can store. The cupboard looks like the start of an apocalypse and feels like a safety net.

prep.l: Get a torch, a crank radio and spare batteries (@18)
prep.txt: A crank radio that works without power, a torch that does too, and a box of batteries. You test each one twice.
Three hours of bandages, recovery positions and compressions on a plastic torso. You leave with a certificate and a lot more confidence.
You practise the evacuation route with your neighbors, a volunteer with a megaphone and a clipboard keeping time. People joke, and then they pay attention.

prep.l: Reinforce your home against local hazards (@60)
prep.txt: Shutters, brackets, straps, a fire extinguisher and a smoke alarm. A day of work, and your home is a harder target for whatever comes.

txt.wonder: You are not hurt, and strangely, you are not afraid. It is just one of those things you will tell people about for years.
txt.nobody: Everyone you care about is accounted for. The relief is physical.
txt.relief: The relief point is running: trucks, volunteers, long lines and hot food.

dispDesc.shelter: A cot in a school gym that smells of disinfectant and damp coats. Someone is crying quietly, and someone else is snoring.
dispDesc.relatives: A spare mattress in {who}'s place. People are kind and cramped, and nobody quite knows where to put their hands.
dispDesc.hotel: A hotel room that costs more than it should, with a muted television and a view of a wall.
dispDesc.tent: A tent in a camp of tents. The ground is hard, the zipper is stuck and the generators never stop.

trauma: A sudden noise, and for a moment you are right back there. Your heart hammers until it fades.
You wake in the dark certain that it is happening again. It is not. It takes a long time to believe that.
You catch yourself checking exits, listening for something. It is exhausting.
tod: in the middle of the morning
